To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cdk2ap suppresses tumor growth and invasion by non-cell-autonmous mechanisms in vitro and in three-way xenografted tumors.

cdk2ap suppresses SCC growth in vivo by altering cell-cell interactions and tumor microenvironment, and that this growth inhibition occurs in part by non-cell-autonomously suppressing tumor cell growth.

cdk2ap 1 expression in the stromal compartment of the tumor microenvironment can reduce SCC growth by altering cell cycle and adhesion gene expression in both cancer cell and stromal cell compartments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of novel genes that can be used to treat head and neck cancer.
identifying and characterizing the molecular mechanisms by which cdk2ap suppresses tumorigenesis.
identifying and characterizing genes and pathways that regulate the tumor microenvironment and tumor cell growth and survival.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cdk2ap suppresses tumor growth in a non-cell-autonomous fashion, and that cdk2 expression may play a role in the regulation of tumor growth and invasion.

cdk2ap suppresses tumor cell phenotypes in vivo and in vitro by both cell-autonomous and non-cell-autonomous effects, and that this suppression can be achieved by expressing cdk 2ap1 in either the tumor cells or the fibroblasts.

the expression of cell cycle regulator, cdk2ap 1 in epithelial cells or stromal cells can reduce tumor growth and invasion, and alter cell cycle, adhesions, invasion, angiogenic, and apoptotic pathways in a non-cell-autonomous fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the expression of a tumor/growth suppressive gene in either the tumor or stromal cell population of an in vitro or in vivo tumor model reduced tumor growth, invasion and angiogenesis.
the cdk2ap gene is a potential therapeutic target for cancer treatment.
cdk2ap suppresses tumor growth by non-cell-autonomously modulating the microenvironment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell cycle regulators such as cdk2ap can be used to target cancer cells and their surrounding stromal cells to suppress tumor growth.
the interactions between epithelial and stromal cells that promote tumor cell growth and invasion can be minimized by cdk2ap gene therapy.
the tumor microenvironment plays a significant role in the development and progression of cancer, and targeting non-cell-autonomous pathways may be a novel strategy in cancer therapy.
